newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa rebounds as sterling eases.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa rebounds as sterling eases.

text.p: London cocoa futures advanced to end sharply higher on fresh trade buying helped by weaker sterling against the dollar, traders said.
"Sterling helped London but I think there's more to it than the currency," said one trader.
The pound was trading at around $1.68950 in late London dealings against around $1.71 late on Tuesday.
Sentiment was also helped by firmer New York cocoa values, news of lower Ghananian cocoa arrivals and a dearth of origin selling as sterling weakened.
Traders said the buying on the sterling-denominated London market was also technically driven after the key March contract broke above the closely-watched chart barrier at 880 stg.
By the close, the most-active contract was 15 stg up at 905 stg a tonne. Traders pegged the next resistance at 910.
Volume was a modest 3,556 lots, with March accounting for the bulk of the turnover.
Ghana's Cocoa Board said cocoa purchases were lower at 11,364 tonnes in the eighth week of the 1996/97 season ending December 5 compared with 18,833 in the same period of the year-earlier season.
Cumulative purchases were 161,270 tonnes at the end of the eighth week compared with 227,491 by December 7, 1995 which corresponded to the ninth week of the 1995/96 season.
Some traders said the news was seen as bullish.
"We feel the arrivals would tail off a bit in the next few weeks," said one.
